verses.zh: 过了一年，到列王出战的时候，大卫又差派约押，率领臣仆和以色列众人出战。他们就打败亚扪人，围攻拉巴。大卫仍住在耶路撒冷。
verses.en: In the spring of the year, at the time when kings[NOTE:1] normally conduct wars,[NOTE:2] David sent out Joab with his officers[NOTE:3] and the entire Israelite army.[NOTE:4] They defeated the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed behind in Jerusalem.[NOTE:5]
notes: Codex Leningrad (B19A), on which BHS is based, has here “messengers” (הַמַּלְאָכִים, hammalʾakhim), probably as the result of contamination from the occurrence of that word in v. 4. The present translation follows most Hebrew mss and the ancient versions, which read “kings” (הַמֶּלָאכִים, hammelakhim).
Heb “go out.”
Heb “and his servants with him.”
Heb “all Israel.”
The disjunctive clause contrasts David’s inactivity with the army’s activity.map For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
11:1 "in the spring" This is literally "at the return of the year." This was the traditional time for military
activities (i.e., the rainy season just over, cf. 1 Kgs. 20;22,26; 1 Chr. 20:1).

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 636, offers the suggestion that the phrase means "a year after
the war of chapter 10 took place."

▣ "when kings go out" Surprisingly the NOUN "kings" (BDB 572 I) is not in the MT but
the spelling of a similar term, "messengers."

- king ‒ מלך

- messenger ‒ מלאך

Although the MT has "messengers," the Masoretic scholars suggested it be read as "kings"
(Qere). The LXX has "Kings."

▣ "But David stayed at Jerusalem" This was very unusual. The king was expected to accompany his troops.

verses.zh: 一日，太阳平西，大卫从床上起来，在王宫的平顶上游行，看见一个妇人沐浴，容貌甚美，
verses.en: One evening David got up from his bed and walked around on the roof of his palace.[NOTE:1] From the roof he saw a woman bathing. Now this woman was very attractive.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “on the roof of the house of the king.” So also in vv. 8, 9.
The disjunctive clause highlights this observation and builds the tension of the story.
verses.commentary:
11:2 "when evening came David arose from his bed" How unusual that David was still in bed at twilight
(i.e., probably about 3 p.m.). Possibly he took a daily nap.

▣ "walked around on the roof" The roof was

- a place to sleep in the warm seasons

- a place to socialize with neighbors

However, the king's palace was higher than the surrounding houses. As he walked on his roof he could
look down into the backyard and rooms of the houses next to the palace.

▣ "he saw a woman bathing" This was not unusual.

- a bath at the end of the day

- a bath in one's

- back yard/courtyard

- a room of the house

- a bath of purification after a woman's period (cf. Lev. 15:19; i.e., to show she was not already pregnant)

Just a word about ceremonial uncleanness. Any bodily fluid made one ceremonially unclean (cf. v. 4).
This has nothing to do with morality but the Israelites' sense of "the holy/sacred." Sex is not an "unclean" act. Sex was
God's design and will for mankind (cf. Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

verses.zh: 大卫就差人打听那妇人是谁。有人说：「她是以连的女儿，赫人乌利亚的妻拔示巴。」
verses.en: So David sent someone to inquire about the woman. The messenger[NOTE:1] said, “Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the messenger) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
11:3 "Bathsheba" Her name could mean

- "daughter of abundance" (BDB 987, possibly Canaanite origin)

- "daughter of an oath" (BDB 989)

- "seventh daughter" (BDB 987 I)

Bathsheba was from a prominent Israeli family.

- grandfather Ahithophel was one of David's trusted advisers, 2 Sam. 15:12; 16:23

- father was one of David's "mighty men," 2 Sam. 23:34

David sinned against both Uriah and Bathsheba's families!

▣ "wife of Uriah the Hittite" This person was a non-Israelite who was part of David's military
(cf. 2 Sam. 23:39). From this account he was an honorable man.

David had many wives (as Nathan would later assert, 2 Sam. 12:1-4) but this was Uriah's only wife.
This was a spur of the moment lust experience (cf. v 2c). This was abuse of power at the highest level (both political
and spiritual).

One MS from the DSS characterizes Uriah as "the armor bearer of Joab," a very important position.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE, C. 4.

verses.zh: 大卫差人去，将妇人接来；那时她的月经才得洁净。她来了，大卫与她同房，她就回家去了。
verses.en: David sent some messengers to get her.[NOTE:1] She came to[NOTE:2] him and he went to bed with her.[NOTE:3] (Now at that time she was in the process of purifying herself from her menstrual uncleanness.)[NOTE:4] Then she returned to her home.
notes: Heb “and David sent messengers and he took her.”

The expression בּוֹא אֶל (boʾ ʾel) means “come to” or “approach,” but is also used as a euphemism for sexual relations, the implied purpose for approaching someone. Here it refers only to the stage of approaching while the next verb describes the result. That she is the subject of this verb (while David is the subject of the next verb) probably indicates that the act was consensual.
Heb “he lay down with her.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakav) “to lie down” can be a euphemism for going to bed for sexual relations.

The parenthetical disjunctive clause further heightens the tension by letting the reader know that Bathsheba, having just completed her menstrual cycle, is ripe for conception. See P. K. McCarter, II Samuel (AB), 286. Since she just had her period, it will also be obvious to those close to the scene that Uriah, who has been away fighting, cannot be the father of the child.
verses.commentary:
11:4 "took her" Bathsheba had no choice or options. The king had ultimate power but in Israel it was from
YHWH for righteous decisions. This was not one!

This sexual abuse/sin will manifest itself in David's family for many generations (i.e., Psalm 32; 51).

- Tamar, rape (cf. 2 Samuel 13)

- Absalom and David's concubines (cf. 2 Sam. 15:16; 16:21-22)

- Solomon's sin with young idolatrous women in his old age (cf. 1 Kgs. 11:1-8)

The NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 102, mentions that the VERB (BDB 1011, KB 1486, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw) denotes an illegal sexual act.

- Lev. 20:11,12,13,18,20

- Deut. 27:20,21,22,23

It denotes "rape" in Gen. 24:2 and Deut. 22:25 or seduction in Gen. 19:23,33 and 35:22.

verses.zh: 于是她怀了孕，打发人去告诉大卫说：「我怀了孕。」
verses.en: The woman conceived and then sent word to David saying, “I’m pregnant.”
verses.commentary:
11:5 Even in David's sin (i.e., which deserved death, cf. Deut. 22:22), YHWH had a redemptive plan. A
child from Bathsheba will be the heir! Not the oldest son, not the rebellious son, but a child of adultery!

verses.zh: 大卫差人到约押那里，说：「你打发赫人乌利亚到我这里来。」约押就打发乌利亚去见大卫。
verses.en: So David sent a message to Joab that said, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” So Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.commentary:
11:6-13 What a shameful account of Uriah's honor and faithfulness vs. David's scheming to deflect the blame
and responsibility.

- call him home so he would have sex with his wife

- get him drunk so he would go home

- have him killed in battle as he fought bravely for David's kingdom

- involved the Israeli army in betrayal, both

- the leadership

- elite soldiers

verses.zh: 乌利亚来了，大卫问约押好，也问兵好，又问争战的事怎样。
verses.en: When Uriah came to him, David asked about how Joab and the army were doing and how the campaign was going.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “concerning the peace of Joab and concerning the peace of the people and concerning the peace of the battle.”

verses.zh: 大卫对乌利亚说：「你回家去，洗洗脚吧！」乌利亚出了王宫，随后王送他一分食物。
verses.en: Then David said to Uriah, “Go down to your home and relax.”[NOTE:1] When Uriah left the palace, the king sent a gift to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and wash your feet.”
Heb “and there went out after him the gift of the king.”
verses.commentary:
11:8 "wash your feet" There are two ways to view this phrase.

- clean yourself and go home to your wife (i.e., a socially/culturally expected thing to do)

- "feet" as a euphemism for male genitalia (cf. Exod. 4:25; Jdgs. 3:24; Ruth 3:4,7,8,14; 1 Sam. 24:3; Isa. 6:2; 7:20)

▣ "a present from the king" This would have been food and drink from David's table.

verses.zh: 乌利亚却和他主人的仆人一同睡在宫门外，没有回家去。
verses.en: But Uriah stayed at the door of the palace with all[NOTE:1] the servants of his lord. He did not go down to his house.
notes: The Lucianic recension of the Old Greek translation lacks the word “all.”

verses.zh: 有人告诉大卫说：「乌利亚没有回家去。」大卫就问乌利亚说：「你从远路上来，为甚么不回家去呢？」
verses.en: So they informed David, “Uriah has not gone down to his house.” So David said to Uriah, “Haven’t you just arrived from a journey? Why haven’t you gone down to your house?”

verses.zh: 乌利亚对大卫说：「约柜和以色列与犹大兵都住在棚里，我主约押和我主（或译：王）的仆人都在田野安营，我岂可回家吃喝、与妻子同寝呢？我敢在王面前起誓（原文是我指着王和王的性命起誓）：我决不行这事！」
verses.en: Uriah replied to David, “The ark and Israel and Judah reside in temporary shelters, and my lord Joab and my lord’s soldiers are camping in the open field. Should I go to my house to eat and drink and go to bed with[NOTE:1] my wife? As surely as you are alive,[NOTE:2] I will not do this thing!”
notes: Heb “lie with.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakav) “to lie down” can be a euphemism for going to bed for sexual relations.
Heb “as you live and as your soul lives.”
verses.commentary:
11:11 "the ark" This strongly implies the ark went into battle against the Ammonites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "lord. . .lord" The word adon (BDB 10) means "owner," "master," "lord," "husband." Here it
denotes Joab and David.

▣

NASB
"By your life and the life of your soul"

NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta
"As you live and as your soul lives"

TEV
"As YHWH lives and you yourself lives"

REB
"By your life"

JPSOA
"As you live, by your very life"

LXX
"How can I? Your soul lives"

The JPSOA footnote suggests an emendation, "As the Lord lives and as
you live" from 1 Sam. 20:3; 25:26. The UBS Text Project, p. 229, gives the MT (NASB close) a "B" rating (some doubt).
However, the oath formula in 1 Samuel fits the context best.

Apparently Uriah viewed this battle as "holy war" and knew the requirements of Deut. 23:9-11; 1 Sam. 21:5.
He was a faithful convert to the Mosaic covenant of YHWH.

verses.zh: 大卫吩咐乌利亚说：「你今日仍住在这里，明日我打发你去。」于是乌利亚那日和次日住在耶路撒冷。
verses.en: So David said to Uriah, “Stay here another day. Tomorrow I will send you back.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem both that day and the following one.[NOTE:1]
notes: On the chronology involved here see P. K. McCarter, II Samuel (AB), 287.

verses.zh: 大卫召了乌利亚来，叫他在自己面前吃喝，使他喝醉。到了晚上，乌利亚出去与他主的仆人一同住宿，还没有回到家里去。
verses.en: Then David summoned him. He ate and drank with him, and got him drunk. But in the evening he went out to sleep on his bed with the servants of his lord; he did not go down to his own house.

verses.zh: 次日早晨，大卫写信与约押，交乌利亚随手带去。
verses.en: In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.

verses.zh: 信内写着说：「要派乌利亚前进，到阵势极险之处，你们便退后，使他被杀。」
verses.en: In the letter he wrote: “Station Uriah at the front in the thick of the battle and then withdraw from him so he will be cut down and killed.”
verses.commentary:
11:15 This premeditated murder of Uriah also involved the death of other innocent Israeli soldiers
(cf. 2 Sam. 11:17-20). Oh my, the sin of the king involved

- the compromise of the army leaders and elite soldiers

- the death of innocent men, in v. 16 they are called "valiant men"

- compromise of the morality of the messengers

- 2 Sam. 11:4

- 2 Sam. 11:19-25

verses.zh: 约押围城的时候，知道敌人那里有勇士，便将乌利亚派在那里。
verses.en: So as Joab kept watch on the city, he stationed Uriah at the place where he knew the best enemy soldiers[NOTE:1] were.
notes: Heb “the valiant men.” This refers in context to the strongest or most valiant defenders of the city Joab and the Israelite army were besieging, so the present translation uses “the best enemy soldiers” for clarity.

verses.zh: 城里的人出来和约押打仗；大卫的仆人中有几个被杀的，赫人乌利亚也死了。
verses.en: When the men of the city came out and fought with Joab, some of David’s soldiers[NOTE:1] fell in battle. Uriah the Hittite also died.
notes: Heb “some of the people from the servants of David.”

verses.zh: 于是，约押差人去将争战的一切事告诉大卫，
verses.en: Then Joab sent a full battle report to David.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Joab sent and related to David all the matters of the battle.”

verses.zh: 又嘱咐使者说：「你把争战的一切事对王说完了，
verses.en: He instructed the messenger as follows: “When you finish giving the battle report to the king,

verses.zh: 王若发怒，问你说：『你们打仗为甚么挨近城墙呢？岂不知敌人必从城上射箭吗？
verses.en: if the king becomes angry and asks you, ‘Why did you go so close to the city to fight? Didn’t you realize they would shoot from the wall?

verses.zh: 从前打死耶路・比设（就是耶路・巴力，见士师记九章一节）儿子亚比米勒的是谁呢？岂不是一个妇人从城上抛下一块上磨石来，打在他身上，他就死在提备斯么？你们为甚么挨近城墙呢？』你就说：『王的仆人―赫人乌利亚也死了。』」
verses.en: Who struck down Abimelech the son of Jerub-Besheth? Didn’t a woman throw an upper millstone[NOTE:1] down on him from the wall so that he died in Thebez? Why did you go so close to the wall?’ just say to him, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.’”
notes: The upper millstone (Heb “millstone of riding”) refers to the heavy circular stone that was commonly rolled over a circular base in order to crush and grind such things as olives.
verses.commentary:
11:21 The death of Ahimelech by a woman throwing stones from the wall of a city is recorded in Jdgs. 9:50-54.

▣ "Jerubbesheth" The LXX and Vulgate have "Jerubbaal" (cf. Jdgs. 7:1, where it refers to Gideon),
while the Peshitta has "Nedo-baal." This is another example of a Hebrew name which included the term "baal" (lord,
owner, master), later changed to "bosheth" (shame) because of the word's later associations with the Canaanite male
fertility god. However, earlier in Israel's history the word was used of YHWH.

verses.zh: 使者起身，来见大卫，照着约押所吩咐他的话奏告大卫。
verses.en: So the messenger departed. When he arrived, he informed David of all the news that Joab had sent with him.

verses.zh: 使者对大卫说：「敌人强过我们，出到郊野与我们打仗，我们追杀他们，直到城门口。
verses.en: The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and attacked us[NOTE:1] in the field. But we forced them to retreat[NOTE:2] all the way to the door of the city gate.
notes: Heb “and came out to us.”
Heb “but we were on them.”

verses.zh: 射箭的从城上射王的仆人，射死几个，赫人乌利亚也死了。」
verses.en: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall and some of the king’s soldiers[NOTE:1] died. Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.”
notes: The translation follows the Qere (“your servants”) rather than the Kethib (“your servant”).
verses.commentary:
11:24 "the archers shot" The MT has no NOUN but two VERBAL forms from the same root.

- "shot" ‒ BDB 432, KB 432, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw (Qere, BDB 434, KB 436)

- "the archers" ‒ BDB 432, KB 432 Hiphil PARTICIPLE (Qere, BDB 434, KB 436, Hiphil
PARTICIPLE)

verses.zh: 王向使者说：「你告诉约押说：『不要因这事愁闷，刀剑或吞灭这人或吞灭那人，没有一定的；你只管竭力攻城，将城倾覆。』可以用这话勉励约押。」
verses.en: David said to the messenger, “Tell Joab, ‘Don’t let this thing upset you.[NOTE:1] There is no way to anticipate whom the sword will cut down.[NOTE:2] Press the battle against the city and conquer[NOTE:3] it.’ Encourage him with these words.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “let not this matter be evil in your eyes.”
Heb “according to this and according to this the sword devours.”
Heb “overthrow.”
The Hebrew text does not have “with these words.” They are supplied in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
11:25 "Do not let this thing displease you" This is a NEGATED IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense. David knew what he did was wrong and tried to rationalize it!

I think this message relates to the valiant soldiers who also died and not to the premeditated death of Uriah.

verses.zh: 乌利亚的妻听见丈夫乌利亚死了，就为他哀哭。
verses.en: When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband Uriah was dead, she mourned for him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for her lord.”
verses.commentary:
11:26 "she mourned for her husband" In 1 Sam 25:39-42 the normal period was one week (i.e., for a father,
also one week, cf. Gen. 50:10).

verses.zh: 哀哭的日子过了，大卫差人将她接到宫里，她就作了大卫的妻，给大卫生了一个儿子。但大卫所行的这事，耶和华甚不喜悦。
verses.en: When the time of mourning passed, David had her brought to his palace.[NOTE:1] She became his wife and she bore him a son. But what David had done upset the Lord.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “David sent and gathered her to his house.”
Heb “and the thing which David had done was evil in the eyes of the Lord.” Note the verbal connection with v. 25. Though David did not regard the matter as evil, the Lord certainly did.
verses.commentary:
11:27 "the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the Lord" The
righteous king was not so righteous. David's abuse of power and lust cast a shadow on the character of YHWH
who chose him as king (cf. 2 Sam. 12:10).

Uriah was a faithful follower of both YHWH and David. It was a sin against hesed.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 11:1

1Then it happened in the spring, at the time when kings go out to battle, that
David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they destroyed the sons of Ammon
and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.
